name: Do I need to replace the entire shower valve, or just the cartridge?

mainEntity.name: Do I need to replace the entire shower valve, or just the cartridge?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, if you're experiencing issues like leaks or temperature control problems, only the shower cartridge needs to be replaced, not the entire valve body. The cartridge is a consumable part designed to be replaced. However, if the valve body itself is corroded, damaged, or severely outdated, then replacing the entire valve might be necessary. A professional assessment can determine the extent of the issue. A key decision factor is the age and condition of the existing valve; a very old or damaged valve may benefit from a full replacement to ensure long-term reliability and compatibility with modern fixtures.
acceptedAnswer.description: Usually, only the cartridge needs replacement. The entire valve is replaced only if it's corroded, damaged, or outdated. A professional assessment determines the best approach.
